comment: Live-site E2E cases for scripts/run-pipeline-tests.ts. category: text|pdf|image|multilang|js|multi. smoke: the per-merge set (npm run test:smoke) — 7 cases chosen 2026-08-09 to cover EVERY format exactly once (text, pdf, image, js, multilang, multi) at ~$0.41, replacing a 3-case set that had no js, multilang or image case and so ran blind to the founder's three most common failures. Three of the seven (De Kas, Vintage Kitchen, Kicky's) are restaurants the ledger shows the Sonnet escalation rung actually rescues, so the set also stress-tests the escalation gate. The full 20-case core set (~$3.00) now runs ONLY on manual dispatch — no schedule, by decision. The six sites added 2026-08-05 (Tofu Vegan, Lina Stores, De Kas, NENI, Waterkant, New King) are the founder-reported 'app can't find an obvious menu' set — the regression guard for the language-switch / JS-overlay / menu-one-hop-deeper / Drive-PDF fixes. Five of them are CORE (not extended) on purpose: these are the patterns that keep regressing, so they run on every merge. The sixth, Waterkant, is EXTENDED for the same reason Amai and Drury are absent — its menu is a Google Drive file the restaurant published view-only ('Sorry, the owner hasn't given you permission to download this file'), so no code change can make it yield a menu and keeping it core would paint main permanently red. It now carries expectBlocked:true, which makes 'reported as blocked, not as no-menu' the PASS condition — the behaviour that IS ours to guard. That also stops it counting as a failure and buying a paid 60s-cooldown re-run of the whole case on every extended run (2026-08-08). If the restaurant ever un-shares the file, this flips to a loud 'expected blocked, got a menu'. Re-check anytime: `npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline-tests.ts waterkant`. NOTE: two of the 7 sites in docs/debug-failed-dublin-restaurants.md (Amai by Viktor, Drury Buildings) are deliberately NOT listed here — their live auto-discovery still fails (Amai: real menu subpages aren't linked anywhere crawlable, not fixable in code; Drury: a TLS trust-chain gap in Node's bundled CA list, expected to self-resolve — see lib/scraper.ts's fetch-fallback comment). Adding them would mean permanently-failing entries with no code fix to chase; the underlying bugs are instead covered by fixtures in tests/discovery.test.ts and tests/scraper-fetch-fallback.test.ts. Re-check either manually anytime: `npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline-tests.ts amai` / `drury`.
